page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by the AMD EPYC 7T83 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz. The instance provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The cache topology provides 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache. It includes standard cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, as well as AVX, BMI2, and FMA flags, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions.

The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware configuration details include zero integrated GPUs and no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for persistent disk state. Network connectivity provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default.

Empirical benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core reaching the top 25% of measured systems. PassMark overall memory testing also lands in the top quartile. However, larger memory transactions show limitations: uncached read bandwidth drops to 38.38 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth registers at 17.58 GB/sec, placing large-block throughput in the bottom 25%. Multi-core compute benchmarks, including a PassMark CPU score of 35,668.95 and Geekbench multi-core score of 11,041.0, place consistently within the middle 50% tier.

From an architectural standpoint, the resource profile emphasizes high memory density without the overhead of specialized accelerators. Workload compatibility centers on large-footprint in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers such as Redis clusters, large ETL pipeline workers, and data analytics tasks where system RAM capacity outweighs raw uncached memory streaming requirements.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor at 2.55 GHz and 256.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, it delivers a memory ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The server includes no GPUs and no onboard local storage, backed by an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks highlight strong single-core compute and high PassMark memory performance, while multi-core workloads and static web serving rank in the middle tier. Uncached large-block memory read and write speeds exhibit lower relative bandwidth. With its dense RAM profile and dedicated CPU cores, ecs.r7a.8xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, enterprise backend services, and large data processing workloads that do not require local NVMe storage.
